goal: WAVE 5: finish every buildable gap with real backend integration on Nano + offline (config_only enforced, buildable not_simulated built, engine-coverage limits lifted)

depth_targets.title: Lifecycle rules (Delete / SetStorageClass actions)
limitations: Age, createdBefore, matchesPrefix/Suffix, matchesStorageClass and the custom-time conditions are evaluated against real object fields and really delete or transition objects (swept lazily on every request against the bucket's objects, not once a day like the real API).
numNewerVersions, daysSinceNoncurrentTime and noncurrentTimeBefore never match — Vyomi keeps no noncurrent object versions to evaluate them against.
The AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload action never fires — Vyomi's resumable-upload sessions carry no persistent "incomplete upload" record to sweep.

depth_targets.title: Bucket IAM policy (getIamPolicy / setIamPolicy), uniform/fine-grained access control, public access prevention
limitations: Policies, the access-control mode and public access prevention round-trip through getIamPolicy/setIamPolicy/buckets.patch exactly as a client sets them, but Vyomi never checks them on a request — every object read/write it allows is unconditional.

depth_targets.title: Insights datasets (Storage Intelligence inventory/usage dataset configs)
limitations: Dataset configs are accepted and listed exactly like the real create/list calls, but Vyomi never runs the underlying export — no BigQuery dataset is populated.
Modeled as a sub-resource of Vyomi's own wire (/storage/v1/insightsDatasets) rather than the real separate storageinsights.googleapis.com service.

depth_targets.title: Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration
limitations: The cors list round-trips through buckets.patch exactly as a client sets it, but Vyomi's wire layer never adds Access-Control-* response headers or blocks a cross-origin browser request — the configuration is not enforced.

depth_targets.title: Static website configuration (main page suffix / 404 page)
limitations: The website config round-trips through buckets.patch exactly as a client sets it, but Vyomi does not run the separate public per-bucket static-website HTTP host (storage.googleapis.com website serving) — the suffix object and 404 page are never actually served.

depth_targets.title: Requester Pays billing
limitations: The billing.requesterPays flag round-trips through buckets.patch exactly as a client sets it, but Vyomi has no billing account or distinct "requester" identity separate from the bucket owner to charge — access is never actually billed to a requester.

depth_targets.title: Object versioning (noncurrent object versions)
limitations: Vyomi's GCS core keeps only the latest generation of an object; it has no store for noncurrent versions, so turning on versioning cannot preserve, list or restore older generations.

depth_targets.title: Soft delete policy (for data recovery)
limitations: Soft delete restores a deleted/overwritten object from its prior generation within a retention window; it depends on the same noncurrent-version history Vyomi does not keep (see gcp.storage.versioning), so a deleted object cannot be recovered.

depth_targets.title: Data encryption with customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK)
limitations: Vyomi always stores object data under Google-managed encryption; selecting a Cloud KMS key is not modeled since the GCS core does not delegate envelope encryption to Cloud KMS on object writes.

depth_targets.title: Hierarchical namespace (HNS buckets with true folders)
limitations: Vyomi's GCS core models every bucket as a flat key-value namespace (folders are zero-byte "name/" placeholder objects); it has no HNS bucket mode with atomic folder rename/delete and folder-level IAM.

depth_targets.title: Resource tags (GCP-wide tag bindings, distinct from labels)
limitations: Tags are bindings against Resource Manager's separate Tags API (tagKeys/tagValues); Vyomi's GCS core has no integration with that service, so tags can't be attached to a bucket.

depth_targets.title: Security insights (bucket column) and Advisor recommendations
limitations: Both are produced by IAM Recommender / Security Command Center analysis and usage-pattern ML over real production traffic; Vyomi runs no such analysis, so it has no findings or recommendations to show.

depth_targets.title: Monitoring (Cloud Monitoring charts: request/error rates, bandwidth)
limitations: Vyomi does not meter per-request traffic over time, so it has no time-series data to chart for request counts, error rates or bandwidth — including the Time range selector and the "Filter by: All locations" control, which have nothing to filter.

depth_targets.title: Long-running bucket operations (rename/relocate bucket, Turbo replication switch)
limitations: Vyomi's bucket operations complete synchronously (see gcp.storage.buckets); it keeps no separate long-running-operation resource to list or poll.

depth_targets.title: Inventory reports (per-bucket Storage Insights object inventory, CSV/Parquet to a destination bucket)
limitations: Inventory reports are a separate Storage Insights sub-product (distinct from gcp.storage.insights-datasets' project-level dataset configs); Vyomi has no report generator to run on a schedule and write CSV/Parquet output to a destination bucket.

depth_targets.title: Object enrichments (Smart Storage — Document AI classification/extraction on upload)
limitations: Enrichments run Document AI (and other Vertex AI pipelines) against newly uploaded objects; Vyomi has no ML inference engine to classify or extract from object content.

depth_targets.title: Interoperable access (HMAC keys for service/user accounts)
limitations: HMAC key issuance is a separate Cloud Storage Interoperability / IAM credentials flow; Vyomi's GCS core has no HMAC keystore or signature verification for the S3-compatible XML API that these keys authenticate against.
